Retail India News: Nykaa Q2 Profit More Than Triples to Rs 101 Cr
BY - Indian Retailer Bureau

Nov 11, 2026 /
1103

FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, reported more than a three-fold increase in consolidated net profit to approximately Rs 101 crore for the second quarter of FY27, ended September 30, 2026. The company had recorded a net profit of around Rs 33 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Consolidated revenue from operations increased 28 percent year-on-year to Rs 3,006 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,345.98 crore in the September quarter of FY26, according to the company's regulatory filing.
Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa said, “Our performance this quarter reflects the strength of the Nykaa ecosystem, with each of our businesses contributing to growth and productivity gains. We continued to improve operational efficiency, particularly across marketing and overheads. Beauty and Fashion are seeing accelerated growth, while House of Nykaa and Wellness offer significant runway for long-term growth. We remain focused on building differentiated businesses that serve our consumers and deliver sustainable growth over the long term.”
The company's beauty business recorded growth during the quarter, supported by new customer additions and increased spending on premium products among existing customers. Nykaa's Beauty vertical reported a gross merchandise value (GMV) of Rs 4,454 crore in Q2 FY27. Its consolidated GMV increased 30 percent year-on-year to Rs 6,151 crore, reflecting growth across its business segments.
The company also reported continued growth in its House of Nykaa portfolio, supported by new product development and category expansion. As part of its portfolio expansion, Nykaa is set to add SimplyNam, a premium professional-grade colour cosmetics brand founded by celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni.
The addition is expected to strengthen Nykaa's presence in the colour cosmetics segment as it continues to expand its beauty brand portfolio. The latest results highlight growth across Nykaa's beauty and fashion businesses, alongside improvements in operational efficiency. The company continues to focus on expanding its beauty, fashion, wellness and owned-brand businesses.

Samiran Tea Strengthens North India Presence With New Noida Office
BY - Indian Retailer Bureau
Sub Editor
Nov 21, 2026

Follow Us
Assam-based tea company Samiran Tea has inaugurated a new office at Bhutani Alphathum, Sector 90, Noida, to strengthen its presence in North India. The inauguration also marked the unveiling of its expanded product portfolio, featuring a 10-variant herbal tea collection, an extended Masala Tea range and Namri Heritage, its premium gifting collection.
Founded in 2006 by Late Naren Sharma, the company aims to use the new office to strengthen relationships with retailers, business partners and consumers across the region while expanding its market presence beyond Assam.
The newly introduced herbal tea collection includes Ayur Slim, Amrit Suddhi, Pachan Shakti, Rakshak Kadha, Arogya Thyro, She Wellness, Ayuu Glow, Nirvana, Gluco Veda and Kashmiri Kahwa. The blends feature ingredients such as moringa, hibiscus, peppermint, lemongrass, ginger, tulsi, amla, ashwagandha, chamomile, lavender and cardamom, offering different flavour combinations and tea-drinking options.
The expanded Masala Tea portfolio comprises Classic Gold Masala Tea, 21 Spices Masala Tea, Herbal Care Gold Masala Tea, Bombay Cutting Masala Tea and Elaichi Tea. The products use Assam CTC tea, with selected variants combining CTC and Orthodox tea. Ingredients across the range include clove, ginger, cardamom, black pepper, cinnamon, fennel, ajwain and tulsi.
Another addition is Namri Heritage, a premium gifting collection named in recognition of the company's founding legacy. It features curated Assam tea assortments in single, three-product and nine-product packs. The offerings include CTC and Orthodox teas, organic green tea, organic Orthodox tea, masala blends and selected flavoured varieties. The collection targets tea enthusiasts and corporate and festive gifting requirements.
Dhiraj Sarmah, Director, Samiran Tea, said: "The inauguration of our Noida office is an important milestone in Samiran Tea's journey. Our roots are firmly connected to Assam, its tea gardens, its people and the vision of my father, Late Naren Sharma, with which this journey began. As we take the brand to new markets, our responsibility is to carry that legacy forward while responding to the changing preferences of consumers. We want people to experience the diversity of Assam tea, the care that goes into its making and the thought behind every blend we introduce. This new office and our expanded portfolio represent the next chapter of that commitment."
Samiran Tea highlights its tea gardens, handcrafted processing and single-origin Assam identity as key aspects of its operations. Its organic range carries NPOP India organic certification, while the company cites 589 laboratory test reports as part of its quality assurance practices.
With the Noida office and expanded portfolio, the company aims to strengthen its regional distribution and reach consumers across traditional teas, herbal blends, masala chai, and premium gifting categories.

Luxury Indian mithai brand Saffron & Mishri is expanding its availability through food delivery platforms Swiggy and Zomato, aiming to reach consumers across multiple locations in Mumbai. The brand will serve customers in Colaba, Worli, Mahalaxmi, Bandra, Santacruz, Andheri, Powai, Kandivali and Borivali, offering its range of Indian sweets, chocolates, savoury products and gifting options.
The expansion is part of the brand's efforts to increase its digital reach and make its products accessible to a wider consumer base. Saffron & Mishri combines traditional Indian sweet-making techniques with contemporary flavours and ingredients, positioning its offerings at the intersection of conventional mithai and modern confectionery.
Its product portfolio includes creations such as Strawberry Matcha Kaju Katli Bar, Dark Chocolate Peda Noir and Kaju Misu Reserve, alongside chocolates and savoury snacks. The brand also offers assorted mithai boxes, festive hampers, gift boxes and additional gifting products such as diyas, catering to celebrations, family gatherings and personal gifting requirements.
Quality and food safety form part of its manufacturing operations. Saffron & Mishri operates through an ISO 22000-certified manufacturing facility and follows quality-control procedures across ingredient sourcing, preparation, and packaging.
Gunjan Shrivastava, Founder, Saffron & Mishri said, “At Saffron & Mishri, our ambition is to take Indian mithai to a global stage, celebrating its extraordinary richness while reimagining it for a contemporary world. We believe Indian mithai has the potential to transcend borders, with its depth of flavour, intricate craftsmanship and remarkable versatility. Through our creations, we bring together the authenticity of Indian culinary traditions with a spirit of innovation, creating experiences that feel both rooted in our heritage and relevant to evolving tastes. Our presence on Swiggy and Zomato is a step towards making our creations more accessible, allowing more people to discover and experience our interpretation of Indian indulgence. While this expansion strengthens our reach across Mumbai, our larger vision extends beyond geographies, to build a brand that introduces Indian mithai to new audiences and earns it a place on the global culinary stage. For us, every new touchpoint is an opportunity to share the artistry of Indian mithai with the world.”
Through its product development strategy, the brand aims to introduce new flavour combinations and formats while retaining traditional mithai-making methods. Its presence on Swiggy and Zomato is expected to strengthen its digital distribution and provide consumers with additional channels to access its products.
The services will cover the identified Mumbai locations, subject to delivery availability on the respective platforms. The company will announce the exact ordering start date and operating hours once finalised.

U.S. Polo Assn. Strengthens India Presence, Contributes 20 Pc to Global Revenue
BY - Indian Retailer Bureau
Sub Editor
Nov 21, 2026
/ 1 MIN READ
Follow Us
U.S. Polo Assn., the official sports brand of the United States Polo Association (USPA), continues to expand its presence in India's apparel market, reporting high-teens growth. The performance reflects the brand's established consumer base and continued demand for its casualwear offerings.
India is currently U.S. Polo Assn.'s third-largest market globally, after the United States and Turkey, and its fastest-growing market. Through its partnership with Arvind Fashions Limited, the brand has developed a strong position in the Indian apparel industry, supported by its retail presence, product portfolio, and consumer reach.
At the global level, U.S. Polo Assn. generated retail sales of US$2.7 billion in 2025. The brand operates across 190 countries, with approximately 1,200 exclusive retail stores and thousands of other distribution points. India accounts for around 20 percent of its global sales, highlighting the country's contribution to its international business.
J. Michael Prince, President, CEO & Board Member USPA Global said, "India has established itself as one of the most important markets in U.S. Polo Assn.'s global business, driven by the strong connection consumers have developed with the brand. Our partnership with Arvind Fashions Limited has played an important role in translating U.S. Polo Assn.'s global identity and heritage into a proposition that resonates with Indian consumers. The brand's performance in India reflects the strength of this partnership, its relevance across consumer segments and the continued demand for quality, versatile apparel."
In India, the brand has built a considerable presence in menswear and is among the country's established sports-casual apparel players. Its product range also includes womenswear, kidswear, footwear, accessories, and underwear. The portfolio focuses on comfort, quality, and versatile styling, while drawing on the brand's association with polo.
U.S. Polo Assn. follows an omnichannel distribution model, reaching customers through exclusive brand outlets, multi-brand stores, department stores and e-commerce platforms. This distribution network allows the company to connect with shoppers through both physical and digital retail channels.
Its growth also supports Arvind Fashions Limited's strategy of increasing direct-to-consumer (D2C) sales. Direct channels currently contribute 53 percent of the company's overall revenue, with a long-term target of taking this share to 65 percent.
Kulin Lalbhai, Vice Chairman and Non-Executive Director, Arvind Fashions Limited, said, "U.S. Polo Assn. has built a strong and enduring connection with Indian consumers over the years, supported by its distinctive brand positioning and ability to remain relevant across generations. Our partnership has been instrumental in translating the brand's global identity into a proposition that resonates with the Indian market. The brand's performance reflects the strength of its consumer franchise, distribution network, and product portfolio. Its established presence across categories and channels has been central to building its scale in India."
The brand is also focusing on marketing initiatives and consumer engagement through strategic associations, advertising campaigns, and collaborations. Its activities featuring Global Brand Ambassador HH Maharaja Sawai Padmanabh Singh (Pacho) further reinforce its association with polo while helping it connect with India's changing apparel consumer base.

Galeries Lafayette Mumbai Marks First Year With La Fête Anniversary Celebration
BY - Indian Retailer Bureau
Sub Editor
Nov 21, 2026
/ 1 MIN READ
Follow Us
Galeries Lafayette Mumbai has completed its first year of operations in India, marking a milestone in the country's luxury retail sector. Established in partnership with Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL), the French department store has built its presence in Mumbai's Kala Ghoda neighbourhood by bringing together international luxury brands, Indian designers and premium lifestyle offerings.
The flagship store features more than 250 Indian and international brands, with 70 percent entering the Indian market exclusively through Galeries Lafayette. Its portfolio spans fashion, beauty, niche fragrances, accessories and home categories, combining established luxury houses, contemporary labels and emerging designers.
The womenswear portfolio includes brands such as Zimmermann, Jacquemus and Gabriela Hearst, while the menswear selection features Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Ami Paris and Balmain. Other labels include CDG PLAY, Represent and NN07. In beauty, the store houses brands such as Hermès Beauty, La Prairie and Diptyque, providing Indian consumers access to a wider range of international luxury offerings.
Sathyajit Radhakrishnan, CEO – Galeries Lafayette India & International Brands, ABFRL said, “Our first year marks the beginning of a larger ambition. As India enters an exciting new phase of luxury consumption, Galeries Lafayette is uniquely positioned to be part of that evolution. We see tremendous potential to shape how consumers discover and experience global luxury. We will continue to broaden our brand portfolio, deepen our presence across categories, and create more meaningful experiences. Our long-term vision is to build a lasting institution that honours the heritage of Galeries Lafayette while evolving with the aspirations of a new generation of luxury consumers.”
Located within the restored Turner Morrison and Voltas House buildings in Kala Ghoda, the store combines heritage architecture with contemporary retail design. Its exterior features Parisian-style canopies, landscaped areas and lighting inspired by the French capital's boulevards.
The interiors, designed by Virgile + Partners, draw inspiration from French Art Deco and modernist architecture, incorporating elements of Indian design such as lotus-inspired structures, pietra dura inlay work and floral patterns. The design brings together the architectural influences of a traditional Parisian Maison Particulière and India's palatial heritage.
Art installations form an integral part of the store's design. The central atrium features the Cupola, a life-size hot air balloon inspired by France's 1796 l’Intrépide. Developed with visual merchandising partner Rare Future, the installation features illustrations from Reshidev R.K.'s Window to Paris series and is positioned alongside the Jardin de Paris spiral staircase.
During its first year, Galeries Lafayette Mumbai hosted several cultural, diplomatic, and fashion-focused events, reflecting its positioning as a platform for international and Indian creative exchanges. The store participated in the Indo-French Year of Innovation and France's Make It Iconic campaign, supporting cultural engagement between the two countries.
Its brand-led activities included the Mumbai debut of a Formula 1 showcar in association with the Monaco Grand Prix, Club Lacoste activities celebrating Roland-Garros and a leather-crafting workshop with Italian luxury brand Serapian. The store also hosted Indian designers Rohit Gandhi + Rahul Khanna for an Evening in Paris fashion presentation and jazz event, bringing Indian design talent into its international retail environment.
Looking ahead, Galeries Lafayette Mumbai plans to expand its brand portfolio and introduce additional international labels in its second year. The retailer is also looking to strengthen its category offerings and develop new experiential formats that provide visitors with greater insight into the craftsmanship and creative processes behind luxury brands.
As part of its first-anniversary celebrations, the store will host La Fête on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Based on the theme The Little Pleasures of Paris, the event will transform different floors of the flagship into spaces inspired by well-known Parisian neighbourhoods, with activities and experiences for visitors.

Nike Targets Threefold Business Growth in India Over Next Five Years
BY - Indian Retailer Bureau
Sub Editor
Nov 19, 2026
/ 1 MIN READ
Follow Us
Global sportswear company Nike is targeting a threefold increase in its India business over the next five years, backed by investments in sportswear, athletic footwear, cricket, running and training. The company is looking to strengthen its position in India's growing sportswear market by expanding consumer engagement and focusing on key sporting categories.
Speaking at Nike's Investor Day, the company's global leadership identified India as a major long-term growth market, citing rising demand for athletic footwear and apparel and the country's expanding sports and fitness ecosystem. According to Cathy Sparks, Vice President and General Manager, Greater China, Nike, India's athletic footwear and apparel market is currently valued at around $9 billion. The market is projected to grow at an annual rate of more than 10 percent, reaching approximately $14 billion by 2031.
“Our ambition is to triple our business in the next five years. We will do that by focusing our resources on running, training and sportswear,” she said.
Cricket will remain a central part of Nike's India growth strategy, given the sport's popularity and its reach across consumer segments. The company plans to connect with athletes at different levels through product development, grassroots initiatives and sporting partnerships.
"You can't win in India without winning in the sport that India loves the most, cricket," Sparks said, adding, “From gully cricket to the pros, we will engage Indian athletes through product innovation, grassroots programmes, and partnerships… ”
Nike's multi-year association with Mumbai Indians across the men's and women's Indian Premier League (IPL) competitions is another part of this strategy. The partnership is expected to provide the company with opportunities to engage cricket audiences across India and international markets. The company is also preparing for cricket's return to the Olympic Games at Los Angeles 2028, following an absence of more than 100 years. As part of its plans, Nike intends to introduce a complete cricket footwear range designed to meet the requirements of the modern game.
“… and when cricket returns to the Olympic Games in LA-28 after more than 100 years, we will be ready with a complete cricket footwear line built for how the game is played today,” she said.
Nike currently offers the Domain 3 cricket shoe for everyday and elite cricket players. The planned expansion of its cricket footwear portfolio is expected to support the brand's presence in the sport as it prepares for the 2028 Olympic Games. Alongside its consumer and product strategy, Nike is making a long-term investment in India through a new campus in Bengaluru. The facility is expected to strengthen the company's capabilities and provide access to India's talent pool, supporting its global business operations.
"India is already an important growth market and manufacturing hub for Nike, with strong capabilities and access to talent. The Bengaluru campus is a long-term investment in new capabilities and talent to strengthen how we serve athletes around the world, including in India," the company had said in a statement last month.
The Bengaluru campus will accommodate full-time employees working across Nike, Jordan Brand and Converse. Existing employees in India will relocate to the facility in phases, while the campus is expected to expand over the coming years.
Nike's India expansion plans are part of a wider global strategy focused on 23 priority markets. These countries have been identified based on their growth potential, opportunities to increase market share and the company's ability to strengthen its position in each market.
According to Sparks, these 23 markets collectively represent nearly 90 percent of Nike's growth opportunity between FY27 and FY31. India's position within this strategy highlights the company's focus on expanding its presence in markets with growing demand for sportswear, athletic footwear and performance apparel.

GUESS JEANS has entered the Indian market with an omnichannel retail strategy, appointing Shoppers Stop as its exclusive national chain store partner. The brand will also be available through its official website, guess.in, and e-commerce platforms including Tata CLiQ, Myntra, AJIO and Nykaa Fashion. The India debut introduces a dedicated denim and lifestyle collection from GUESS JEANS, the youth-focused sub-brand within the GUESS portfolio.
The entry follows GUESS's arrival in India in 2025 and marks another step in the company's expansion in the country's fashion and apparel market. Drawing on the group's 45-year denim heritage, GUESS JEANS is targeting younger consumers with a collection influenced by international streetwear, Y2K fashion and Korean style. The range features relaxed denim silhouettes, graphic elements and everyday apparel designed around contemporary fashion preferences.
The brand has also appointed Hyunjin of K-pop group Stray Kids as its global brand ambassador. His association with the campaign connects the brand's India entry with its wider positioning across international music, fashion and youth culture. Alongside its online distribution network, GUESS JEANS will be available through select shop-in-shop locations at Shoppers Stop, Kapsons International and Iconic Fashion across major Indian cities. The distribution strategy combines department store retail, multi-brand fashion outlets and e-commerce channels to increase the brand's reach among Indian consumers.
Ajay Kumar, Country Manager, GUESS India said, "The launch of GUESS JEANS in India is an important milestone in our journey to connect with a new generation of consumers. Our collaborations with Shoppers Stop and Tata CLiQ are key to this ambition, bringing together a strong physical retail presence and digital reach. Through these partnerships, we aim to make GUESS JEANS' distinctive denim heritage and contemporary, youth-focused style more accessible to Indian consumers, wherever they choose to shop."
Kavindra Mishra, Managing Director and CEO, Shoppers Stop said, "At Shoppers Stop, our focus has always been on bringing globally recognised brands closer to discerning Indian consumers through a curated retail experience. Our partnership with GUESS JEANS strengthens this proposition by giving customers the opportunity to discover the brand across our department store network. As the exclusive national chain store for GUESS JEANS in India, we are pleased to bring its distinctive denim and contemporary fashion offering to our customers. This partnership further strengthens our international brand portfolio while creating a differentiated experience for customers across our stores."
Gopal Asthana, CEO, Tata CLiQ said, "At Tata CLiQ, apparel is one of our leading categories. We have a strong and curated portfolio of brands catering to diverse consumer preferences across both our platforms. With GUESS JEANS, we continue to expand our offerings, bringing customers their styles that combine timeless appeal with contemporary design."
GUESS JEANS was globally introduced in 2024, with Nicolai Marciano overseeing international brand activations, flagship store openings and cultural partnerships across Los Angeles, Tokyo, Berlin and Amsterdam. These initiatives have focused on building the brand's presence across fashion, art and music.
The India entry extends this international expansion into another major fashion market. Through partnerships with Shoppers Stop and Tata CLiQ, alongside other retail and e-commerce channels, GUESS JEANS is establishing a distribution network that combines physical stores with digital sales platforms. The brand is expected to expand its presence through future collections, collaborations and retail initiatives.

Mitra FMCG and Tanvi Foods Announce Rs 600 Cr Integration
BY - Indian Retailer Bureau
Sub Editor
Nov 19, 2026
/ 1 MIN READ
Follow Us
Mitra FMCG and BSE-listed Tanvi Foods (India) Limited have announced a strategic integration valued at Rs 600 crore, with Bestvantage Investments acting as the exclusive advisor to the transaction. The integration aims to combine the companies' capabilities across food processing, agricultural sourcing, procurement and distribution, while creating opportunities for business expansion in India and overseas markets.
The integration is expected to strengthen Mitra FMCG's farm-to-fork business model by bringing together sourcing, procurement and distribution operations. An important area of focus will be the use of Tanvi Foods' existing export network to help Mitra expand its presence in international markets, including the United States, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.
Abhishek Kaushik, Founder of Mitra FMCG said, “This strategic integration marks an important milestone in Mitra's growth journey. By bringing together our complementary strengths with Tanvi Foods, we aim to strengthen our presence across the value chain, expand our domestic and international reach, and build a more scalable farm-to-fork business. We see this as an opportunity to create long-term value through stronger sourcing, efficient supply chains and a wider market presence.”
The partnership will also focus on strengthening the companies' distribution networks across different regions of India. Mitra FMCG's distribution capabilities are expected to help Tanvi Foods expand its reach across Northern India. In return, Tanvi Foods' market access and operational infrastructure will support Mitra's growth in Southern India, particularly in the household essentials category.
Another key area of the integration will be raw material sourcing. Tanvi Foods will gain access to essential inputs such as flour, refined flour (maida) and edible oils through Mitra FMCG's procurement network. This arrangement is expected to improve procurement efficiencies, optimise costs and strengthen supply-chain operations for the businesses.
The Rs 600 crore integration is aimed at creating a more connected business structure by combining the companies' respective strengths in food processing, sourcing and distribution. The arrangement is also expected to help both businesses reach new customer segments, strengthen their domestic operations and explore additional opportunities in international food markets.
For the Indian FMCG and food processing sectors, the integration highlights the growing importance of supply-chain capabilities, regional distribution networks and export infrastructure in supporting business expansion.

According to the report, India’s electronics market is expected to grow from approximately ₹7 trillion in 2024 to ₹10 trillion by 2030. Device upgrades are expected to account for a significant share of the incremental ₹3 trillion opportunity, alongside first-time adoption in underpenetrated markets.
Smaller cities emerge as growth drivers
The report highlights a significant shift in India’s electronics consumption, with non-metro markets recording faster growth than metros.
Between 2022 and 2025, Croma’s sales grew at a 40% CAGR in Tier III cities, 30% in Tier II cities and 35% in Tier I cities, compared with 13% in metros.
As a result, the share of Croma’s sales coming from non-metro markets increased from 32% in 2022 to 44% in 2025. While metros continue to contribute higher absolute demand, the faster growth in smaller cities is making them increasingly important to the next phase of electronics consumption.
“Over the last two decades, we have witnessed India's consumer-electronics market evolve from first-time adoption to being shaped by aspiration, experience and continual upgrading,” said Shibashish Roy, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, Infiniti Retail Ltd. (Croma).
He added that as technology becomes more sophisticated, Croma’s focus is on simplifying electronics ownership through product choice, expert advice, affordability solutions and after-sales support.
Indian consumers are trading up
Premiumisation is emerging as another key driver of the electronics market.
At Croma, the average smartphone selling price increased 34% between 2021 and 2025, while smartphones priced above ₹50,000 recorded a 26% CAGR in value between 2022 and 2025.
The trend is also visible across large appliances and televisions. Inverter ACs accounted for 91% of the category at Croma in 2025, compared with just 9% in 2015, indicating a shift from premium features towards mainstream adoption.
Meanwhile, larger television screens are gaining traction. One in three televisions sold at Croma in 2025 measured 55 inches or larger, compared with one in 25 in 2015.
New categories enter Indian homes
The report also identifies several emerging categories that are gaining consumer acceptance.
At Croma, dishwashers and dryers together recorded a 29% volume CAGR between 2021 and 2025. Gaming devices recorded a 26% volume CAGR, while hearables such as headphones and earbuds grew 23% and air fryers grew 22% during the same period.
These categories are expected to play a larger role in India’s next consumption cycle as households move beyond essential electronics towards convenience, entertainment and lifestyle-led technology.
“ The future of India’s consumer-electronics industry will be shaped not by how many devices are sold, but by how consumers choose to upgrade their lives through technology,” said Kaushika Madhavan, Chairman, Kearney India.
She added that premiumisation, expanding demand across emerging markets and evolving consumer expectations are creating opportunities for innovation, value creation and long-term growth.
Croma expands omnichannel footprint
Croma currently operates more than 560 stores across over 200 cities and continues to expand its physical retail network. Its omnichannel ecosystem also includes its website, Tata Neu and BigBasket.
The retailer is using its 20-year journey to position itself for the next phase of electronics consumption, as Indian consumers increasingly upgrade existing devices, adopt new categories and expand their electronics purchases beyond major metropolitan markets.

Founded by entrepreneur and watch enthusiast Endre Szakacs, Cook & Re aims to build its identity around the philosophy of “Challenge Over Comfort”, drawing inspiration from Dubai’s entrepreneurial and challenger mindset while combining it with Swiss watchmaking expertise.
The SUPRA 42 marks the brand’s first release, with the first 50 buyers positioned as the brand’s inaugural “Conquerors”, a community of individuals united by their pursuit of personal and professional challenges.
“I didn’t want to create another watch that simply tells the time. I wanted to create something that reminds you what time actually means. The countdown started the day you were born. What matters is what you do before it runs out,” said Szakacs.
Watch Design Inspired by Time and Challenge
A key design element of the SUPRA 42 is its Memento Mori-inspired power reserve, presented in blood red to indicate the mechanical energy remaining in the movement. The dial incorporates topographic contour-line detailing, drawing inspiration from maps used by climbers and mountaineers before attempting a summit.
The watch features a 42mm case made from 316L marine-grade stainless steel, a unidirectional bezel and water resistance of up to 200 metres. The first edition is available in Falcon Black and comes with an interchangeable strap featuring the brand's signature red-and-white striped motif.
Conceived in Dubai and manufactured in Switzerland, the SUPRA 42 combines the brand's UAE origins with Swiss precision and mechanical watchmaking.
Building a Watch Brand as an Outsider
Szakacs brings more than two decades of experience in international banking across Hungary, the UK and the Gulf to the venture. His interest in watches began during childhood, when he would take apart alarm clocks and sleep with a wristwatch beside him to listen to its movement.
The loss of his father eventually prompted Szakacs to turn that long-standing fascination into a business built around the concept of limited time and personal achievement.
“No watchmaking background. No connections in Switzerland. Zero excuses. I chose the impossible path: to build a Swiss-made watch from Dubai. Not because I knew how. Because the challenge demanded it from me,” said Szakacs.
Rather than positioning the brand around traditional luxury credentials and heritage, Cook & Re aims to focus on craftsmanship, personal achievement and storytelling.
Limited to 50 Pieces
The company is limiting its first edition to 50 watches, with each piece individually numbered. The brand said it intends to maintain scarcity without relying on artificial waiting lists or traditional luxury status cues.
“We are not interested in creating waiting lists for the sake of waiting lists. If something is genuinely rare, it doesn’t need games around its scarcity. There are 50 watches available within this first release. When they are gone, they are gone,” Szakacs said.
Beyond the first collection, Cook & Re plans to build its brand around personal challenge, community and storytelling, with future watches continuing to explore its “Challenge Over Comfort” philosophy.

HomeLane and DesignCafe, two home interior brands owned by parent company Homevista, have collectively expanded their retail footprint to 100 Experience Centres across 43 cities in India. The development marks a key milestone in the company's expansion strategy as it looks to increase access to organised home interior solutions across the country. With more than 70,000 homes delivered, Homevista is strengthening its physical retail presence to reach a wider customer base. The expansion brings together HomeLane's technology-enabled, end-to-end home interior services and DesignCafe's architect-led, personalised design solutions under a shared retail network.
The two brands are following different expansion strategies to reach customers across markets. While HomeLane is increasing its presence in emerging cities, DesignCafe is expanding in growing urban markets, including Gandhinagar and Surat. Both businesses leverage shared technology, manufacturing and execution infrastructure to support their operations. The expansion also addresses the growing importance of physical experience centres in the home interior market. Since home interior purchases involve significant investment and long-term decisions, customers often prefer visiting studios to explore materials, understand design options and interact with designers before finalising projects. Through its expanding network, Homevista aims to make professional design consultations and 3D home visualisation services accessible to more homeowners across India.
All 100 Experience Centres have been funded by franchise partners, reflecting Homevista's focus on local entrepreneurship as part of its retail expansion strategy. Most of the centres operate under the Franchise-Owned, Company-Operated (FOCO) model, where franchise partners invest in the studios while the respective brands handle daily operations. HomeLane has also been expanding its presence in smaller cities through the Franchise-Owned, Franchise-Operated (FOFO) model. Under this arrangement, local entrepreneurs invest in and manage the studios.
Both franchise formats provide partners access to the brands' technology platforms, product catalogues, manufacturing facilities and supply chain infrastructure. The model allows Homevista to expand its retail network while maintaining consistency in customer experience and project execution. HomeLane's presence now includes cities such as Jamshedpur, Udaipur, Nagercoil, Ranchi, Bhilai and Latur. The company plans to double its FOFO network over the next six months.
Tanuj Choudhry, Co-Founder and COO of HomeLane said, “Home interiors is a category where being close to the customer really matters. Our 100 Experience Centres make it easier for families to experience products, meet designers and plan their homes with confidence. We’ve always believed in building our retail network with local entrepreneurs, supported by strong technology and execution capabilities. The opportunity to take this model deeper into India is enormous.”
The franchise model has also enabled individual partners to expand their businesses. In Jamshedpur, Roshan Agarwal, HomeLane's first FOFO franchise partner at Bindal Mall, has completed more than 65 projects in nearly three years and subsequently invested in a second studio.
Roshan Agarwal said, “We’ve built a business with healthy returns and consistent growth. HomeLane’s focus on quality, innovation and an expanding product range has helped us serve customers with hassle-free, turnkey interiors. The success of our first studio gave us the confidence to invest in a second.”
While operating under the same parent company, HomeLane and DesignCafe cater to homeowners through different service propositions. HomeLane focuses on end-to-end home interior solutions supported by technology, transparent pricing and professional project execution. Its proprietary SpaceCraft platform offers 3D design visualisation and real-time pricing to help customers plan their interiors.
The brand also offers a 45-day delivery guarantee and a 10-year material warranty, subject to applicable terms. DesignCafe, meanwhile, operates a network of 23 Experience Centres and focuses on architect-led interior design, personalised layouts and space optimisation. Its approach centres on understanding household requirements and developing designs based on individual lifestyles and functional needs.
Gita Ramanan, Co-Founder and CEO of DesignCafe said, “At DesignCafe, our design DNA starts with a simple question: how does this family actually live? Where do the adults work and where do the children study? How is the wardrobe used, who cooks, and where does everyone gather once the day is done? Those answers are why no two DesignCafe homes are alike, and why everyday living feels more thoughtful, functional and personal. Our growing network lets us bring this approach to more homeowners across India.”
With a combined network of 100 Experience Centres, Homevista is continuing to expand its presence in India's organised home interiors market. Its franchise-led approach, supported by two distinct brands, is aimed at reaching customers in both established urban markets and smaller cities.

JSW Dulux Limited, formerly Akzo Nobel India Limited, reported a 21 percent increase in sales volume for the second quarter of FY27, with revenue from operations rising 21.3 percent to Rs 961.9 crore on a comparable standalone basis. The company's board approved the financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. For Q2 FY27, EBITDA from operations increased 4.4 percent to Rs 110.9 crore, compared with Rs 106.3 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Profit after tax (PAT), excluding exceptional items, grew 2 percent to Rs 71.2 crore from Rs 69.8 crore. For the first half of FY27, the company recorded 23 percent volume growth, while comparable revenue from operations increased 20 percent to Rs 1,926.9 crore against Rs 1,605.3 crore in H1 FY26. EBITDA from operations rose 9.4 percent to Rs 226 crore, while PAT excluding exceptional items increased 50.5 percent to Rs 206.7 crore from Rs 137.3 crore.
The comparable figures relate to the retained business and exclude the business carved out in the previous year. The company said the previous year's comparable figures are provisional, unaudited and based on management estimates. The H1 FY27 PAT also includes dividend income of Rs 55.9 crore from its subsidiary, ICI India Research and Technology Centre Private Limited, following a dividend of Rs 447 per equity share.
On a reported standalone basis, JSW Dulux's Q2 FY27 revenue from operations increased 16.2 percent to Rs 961.9 crore from Rs 827.6 crore. EBITDA from operations rose marginally by 0.3 percent to Rs 110.9 crore. PAT stood at Rs 71.2 crore, compared with Rs 1,682.7 crore in Q2 FY26, which included exceptional items of Rs 1,874.2 crore before tax from the sale of the Powder Coatings business, IRC and related costs.
For H1 FY27, reported revenue from operations grew 5.8 percent to Rs 1,926.9 crore from Rs 1,820.7 crore. EBITDA from operations declined 7.8 percent to Rs 226 crore, compared with Rs 245.1 crore in the year-ago period. PAT was Rs 206.7 crore, against Rs 1,773.7 crore in H1 FY26, which included the same exceptional items.
Rajiv Rajgopal, Joint Managing Director and CEO, JSW Dulux Ltd said, “We delivered consecutive quarter of double-digit volume and value growth, reflecting steady progress on our strategic priorities. We continued to make steady market share gains across our businesses. In Decorative Paints, all categories witnessed strong traction leading up to the festive season. Industrial Paints performance was aided by strong demand in infrastructure and energy sectors. We saw gains in automotive space with customer wins and entry into new verticals. While raw material inflation remains elevated, we have undertaken calibrated price increases to partly offset margin dilution. Despite these headwinds, comparable EBITDA grew 4.4 percent through prudent balance between cost management and growth initiatives. However, as geopolitical disturbances continue to affect raw material inflation, we will keep evaluating the situation and implementing calibrated price increases.”
During the quarter, shareholders approved a proposal to subdivide the company's equity shares in a 10:1 ratio, reducing the face value from Rs 10 per share to Re 1 per share. The subdivision took effect for stock exchange trading following the record date of October 22, 2026. In its decorative paints business, the company introduced VT Soft Sheen across India under its Accessible Luxury portfolio. The product combines the TruColour proposition with an eight-year Dulux Assurance warranty.
JSW Dulux also expanded its automotive and specialty coatings portfolio with the introduction of the EONIX Rubbing and Polishing Compound range. The products mark the brand's entry into adjacent categories within OEM-authorised workshop networks and are aimed at surface correction and finishing applications in the automotive refinish segment.
The company said demand in decorative paints was supported by customer activity ahead of the festive season, while its industrial paints business benefited from demand in the infrastructure and energy sectors. Its automotive coatings business also reported customer additions and entry into new market segments. However, higher raw material costs continued to put pressure on margins, prompting the company to implement calibrated price increases.

Swiggy has introduced battery-swapping stations at its Instamart pods across 25 locations as part of its efforts to expand electric vehicle adoption in last-mile delivery. The initiative was announced at the company's EV Mobility Conclave, themed “Powering the last mile”, attended by Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari.
The conclave brought together electric vehicle manufacturers, charging and battery-swapping companies, fleet operators, rental service providers, financiers and delivery partners to discuss ways to make electric two-wheelers more accessible and affordable for last-mile delivery operations. Alongside the battery-swapping network, Swiggy is introducing EV rental services at its Instamart pods. The arrangement will allow delivery partners to rent electric two-wheelers from the same locations where they collect orders, reducing the need to travel elsewhere to access a vehicle or charging facility.
Sriharsha Majety, Co-Founder and Group CEO, Swiggy said, “Every order has a person behind it, and the last mile is that person. Our delivery partners are at the heart of everything we do, and our vision is to make their work easier and more rewarding. For those who choose electric, that means taking away the everyday hurdles, so that the transition fits naturally into the way they already work. When a solution is built around the partner’s day rather than around the technology, adoption becomes a natural choice. That is the future we want to help build for the people who power India’s last mile.”
According to the company, a delivery partner may visit an Instamart pod around 20 times on a busy day. By placing EV rental and battery-swapping facilities at these locations, Swiggy aims to reduce the time delivery partners spend travelling to separate charging or vehicle collection points. The saved time can be used to complete more orders or for personal activities.
Neha Singhvi, Head of Corporate Affairs, Swiggy said, “EV adoption in last-mile delivery depends on enablers that sit beyond any one platform. Affordable financing, reliable charging and swapping, and supportive policy. Many of the partners honoured today have worked on exactly these challenges, and their experience is valuable to the wider ecosystem. We value the government's continued engagement, and we look forward to working with industry and policymakers on solutions that help partners who choose EVs.”
The event also recognised delivery partners who have adopted electric vehicles, along with companies contributing to EV infrastructure and mobility services. The ecosystem partners honoured included Indofast Energy, Yulu, Bounce Daily, RIDEV, Baaz Bikes, Motovolt, Shadowfax, BGauss Auto, Veelo Mobility, Hala Mobility and Yuma Energy. Delivery partners Sajan Lal, Kamal Kumar, Avanish, Sandeep Gupta, Vijay, Ritik and Khurshid were also recognised.
Varun Agni, Co-Founder and CTO, Bounce said, “Access to a vehicle is one of the biggest barriers for anyone who wants to do delivery work. A large number of our riders had no vehicle of their own before they started with us. With this partnership, a rider has access to an affordable EV the moment they need one for work, and the battery-swapping infrastructure is already in place. The time, effort and money that saves contributes directly to a riders daily earnings and can help in meeting customer demand more efficiently. This is a big win for the ecosystem - for riders and customers both.”
An EV delivery partner, Umesh said, “I rented an EV using the Swiggy app at affordable charges which were deducted from my payouts as per my preference. The battery swapping can also be easily done at the Instamart pods when I go to pick an order, ensuring I can make the most of my day and earn more.”
Nitin Gadkari, Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India said, "India's growth depends on clean, efficient and affordable transport. Delivery partners are the backbone of the new economy, and when they choose electric vehicles, it benefits their incomes, our cities and our environment. I appreciate Swiggy and its partners for working together to bring practical solutions closer to those who need them. Government and industry must continue to collaborate so that every delivery partner who wants to choose an EV finds it easy to do so."
The initiative brings together EV rentals and battery-swapping infrastructure at locations already used by delivery partners, addressing two practical requirements for electric mobility in the delivery sector: vehicle access and battery availability.

Standalone PAT stood at Rs 6.1 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 4.8 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated total income increased 26.5 percent to Rs 891 crore, while EBITDA rose 124.6 percent to Rs 104 crore. The company reported a consolidated PAT of Rs 26.5 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 22.9 crore in H1 FY26. Standalone total income for the six-month period grew 30.1 percent to Rs 713.5 crore, while EBITDA increased 49.2 percent to Rs 68.6 crore. Standalone PAT rose to Rs 20.6 crore from Rs 4.8 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Arvind Singhania, Chairman, Ester Industries said, "Improvement witnessed in Q1FY27 continued during Q2FY27 with improving operating environment, higher realizations, increased throughput and a favorable product mix. Consolidated Total Income increased 25.7 percent Y-o-Y to Rs 449.0 crores, while EBITDA more than doubled, rising 160 percent Y-o-Y to Rs 45.1 crore. EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 10 percent from 4.9 percent in Q2FY26, reflecting improved operating performance and better business mix resulting from higher contribution of Value-Added products within Film segment and better realizations across product portfolio. PAT turned positive at Rs 7.80 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 15.8 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The operating environment for the BOPET Film industry remained stable during Q2 FY27, with the US tariff-related disruptions witnessed in FY26, largely behind us. However, disruptions in crude oil supply and price fluctuations caused by war in West Asia are resulting into higher shipping costs and longer transit time which is adversely impacting working capital cycle.”
"In Specialty Polymers, sales volume was 711 MT in Q2FY27 against 1,161 MT in Q2 FY26, however segment EBIT margin remained healthy at 33.9 percent. Though one of the marquee products in Specialty Polymers SBU has seen demand erosion but basis the strong product pipeline, and expected customer approval for a new product post marginal capital expenditure in near future is expected to partially make good the lost sales volume and margins. Our performance reflects the strength of our strategy, the resilience of our business and our relentless focus. However, the global geopolitical environment remains uncertain, creating challenges for raw material costs and pricing visibility.”
"Looking ahead, we remain confident about Ester’s medium to long-term growth prospects, supported by improving industry conditions, favorable regulatory tailwinds and its continued focus on premium and Value-Added products. The increasing focus on differentiated products is expected to provide greater resilience across industry cycles and support sustainable margin improvement over the medium to long term. By focusing on operational efficiency, capacity utilization and advanced Specialty products, the company remains committed to driving profitability growth and reducing its environmental footprints.”
"As regard to ELITe project, we are glad to inform that various aspects related to implementation of the project by last quarter of CY 2028 are progressing well with acquisition of land expected to be completed by Q4FY27. Marketing and Off Take agreement with an anchor customer coupled with a Letter of Intent secured from a leading global sports and athletic brand for Loop PET Fiber Grade resin, under a multi-year framework for offtake from its upcoming Gujarat facility would ensure that a significant portion of the planned capacity gets committed ahead of commercial production. This early customer validation provides strong visibility for the JV’s recycled platform and underscores the growing demand for its Value-Added, sustainable product offerings."
In the polyester films business, consolidated capacity utilisation reached 92 percent in Q2 FY27, compared with 80 percent in the year-ago quarter. Film sales volume increased 13.9 percent to 24,291 MT from 21,329 MT, while revenue grew 39.6 percent to Rs 414.5 crore against Rs 296.8 crore in Q2 FY26. The increase in revenue was supported by higher per-unit realisations following a rise in petrochemical feedstock prices. Ester Industries continued to increase its focus on value-added and specialty (VAS) films. Sales of these products reached 6,200 MT, accounting for 25.3 percent of total film sales volume. VAS volumes grew 25.8 percent from 4,927 MT in the corresponding quarter last year. Recycled PET (rPET) sales volume increased 37.4 percent to 1,437 MT, while revenue rose 51 percent to Rs 18.4 crore.
The specialty polymers segment recorded sales volume of 711 MT in Q2 FY27, down 38.8 percent from 1,161 MT in Q2 FY26. Despite the lower volume, the segment reported an EBIT margin of 33.9 percent. The company attributed the decline in sales to demand erosion in one of its key specialty polymer products and expects new product approvals to help recover part of the lost volumes and margins.
Ester Industries is also progressing with its ELITe project, which is targeted for implementation by the last quarter of calendar year 2028. Land acquisition is expected to be completed by Q4 FY27. The company has secured a marketing and offtake agreement with an anchor customer, along with a Letter of Intent from a global sports and athletic brand for Loop PET Fiber Grade resin from the proposed Gujarat facility. The multi-year arrangement is expected to secure a significant share of the facility’s planned capacity before commercial production begins.

Supply operations are expected to begin shortly, with the company targeting product availability across V2 Retail's entire store network by mid-December 2026. The arrangement is part of Cupid's strategy to expand its domestic fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) business and increase its presence in organised retail. By using V2 Retail's existing store network, Cupid will be able to expand its physical distribution without independently setting up a comparable retail infrastructure.
The agreement will also extend to new stores opened by V2 Retail, allowing Cupid to increase its retail presence as the fashion retailer expands its network. The companies plan to introduce additional products and categories through the dedicated retail spaces over time.
Aditya Kumar Halwasiya, Chairman and Managing Director of Cupid Limited said, "This is a landmark and transformative development for Cupid Limited and represents one of the most important milestones in the evolution of our domestic consumer business. Our long-term exclusive arrangement with V2 Retail provides Cupid with something exceptionally valuable: a dedicated, large-scale, nationwide retail platform with visibility across both the existing store network and all future expansion. With 400 square feet of exclusive retail space in every V2 Retail store, we are creating a powerful consumer-facing distribution ecosystem capable of supporting a rapidly expanding portfolio of personal care and wellness products. We expect this partnership to generate approximately Rs 400 crore in revenue within the next 12 months."
Ram Chandra Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director of V2 Retail Limited said, "We are delighted to enter into this long-term strategic arrangement with Cupid Limited, a company that is rapidly establishing itself as a strong and trusted Indian brand in the personal care and wellness segment. Cupid's growing portfolio of high-quality personal care and wellness products will significantly strengthen our in-store offerings and allow us to provide our customers with superior-quality products at highly compelling price points. The Rs 400 crore revenue estimate represents management's expectation for the next 12 months and will depend on the pace of the rollout, consumer demand, product availability and business performance. For Cupid, the partnership provides access to an established organised retail network to expand its domestic FMCG and consumer wellness portfolio. For V2 Retail, the arrangement will add dedicated personal care and hygiene offerings to its existing product assortment. The rollout and sales generated through the stores will determine how significantly the partnership contributes to both companies' business growth.
